checkpoints.question: According to NIST SP 800-63B, what is the recommended minimum password length?

options.A: Minimum 6 characters with at least one uppercase letter required
options.B: Minimum 8 characters with support for at least 64 characters allowed
options.C: Minimum 10 characters with mixed character types required
options.D: Minimum 12 characters with numbers and symbols both required

checkpoints.explanation: NIST SP 800-63B explicitly recommends a minimum of 8 characters and allowing up to at least 64 characters. Length is prioritized over complexity requirements.

checkpoints.question: What does NIST 800-63B recommend instead of rigid complexity requirements?

options.A: Enforce uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and special character rules
options.B: Enforce numbers and special characters at specific position requirements
options.C: Enforce monthly password changes combined with complexity requirements
options.D: Enforce length requirements and block commonly used or compromised passwords

checkpoints.explanation: The section states that NIST prefers requiring length and prohibiting commonly used or compromised passwords, rather than rigid complexity rules which produce predictable patterns.

checkpoints.question: According to NIST 800-63B, when should users be required to change their passwords?

options.A: Quarterly along with security awareness training
options.B: Every 90 days as part of routine maintenance
options.C: When compromise is known or suspected only

checkpoints.explanation: NIST 800-63B recommends not forcing periodic expiration; instead, organizations should only require immediate change when compromise is known or suspected.

checkpoints.question: What does the observation window parameter in an account lockout policy control?

options.A: The time period within which consecutive failures are counted
options.B: The duration the account remains locked after reaching the threshold
options.C: How long the administrator must wait before resetting an account
options.D: The total number of login attempts allowed per day

checkpoints.explanation: The section defines the observation window as the time period within which failures are counted before triggering a lockout, typically 10–30 minutes.

checkpoints.section: Password managers: the practical fix for humans
checkpoints.question: What anti-phishing benefit do password managers provide through their autofill function?

options.A: They block access to websites with known vulnerabilities or weaknesses
options.B: They encrypt all network traffic between the user and the target website
options.C: They warn users when visiting unencrypted or suspicious websites
options.D: They verify the actual domain and refuse to fill credentials on lookalike phishing sites

checkpoints.explanation: The section states that the autofill function checks the actual domain and will not fill credentials on a lookalike phishing page with a different domain.

checkpoints.question: Why are MD5 and SHA-1 unsuitable for password hashing?

options.A: They prioritize speed over security and allow rapid brute-force password testing
options.B: They produce hashes that are too short for adequate security
options.C: They require salts that are too expensive or difficult to generate properly
options.D: They cannot integrate with modern database systems or applications

checkpoints.explanation: The section explains that MD5 and SHA-1 are general-purpose hash functions designed for speed, which lets attackers test billions of guesses per second with GPU hardware.

checkpoints.question: What makes Argon2id the recommended choice for password hashing in new systems?

options.A: It is faster than competing algorithms and requires no configuration
options.B: It was the first algorithm designed specifically for password storage
options.C: It combines GPU resistance and side-channel resistance with tunable parameters
options.D: It requires no salt and automatically protects against rainbow table attacks

checkpoints.explanation: Argon2id is described as the winner of the 2015 Password Hashing Competition that combines GPU resistance and side-channel resistance; it is recommended for general use with tunable iteration count, memory, and parallelism.

checkpoints.question: How does PAM (Privileged Access Management) prevent reuse of harvested privileged credentials?

options.A: It logs all administrative activity and generates alerts on suspicious behavior
options.B: It automatically rotates passwords after each use so current credentials remain unknown
options.C: It stores passwords in an encrypted vault protected by a master password
options.D: It requires multi-factor authentication for every privileged account access attempt

checkpoints.explanation: The section states that PAM rotates passwords automatically after each use and no individual ever knows the current credential, preventing reuse of harvested credentials.
